akhfash:15-16.t: He said ﴿كَلاَّ إِنَّهَا لَظَىٰ﴾ ﴿نَزَّاعَةً لِّلشَّوَىٰ﴾: accusative as a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ (the pronoun)**, and the khabar (predicate) of "إنَّ" is ﴿نزَاعةٌ﴾. «[Translator's note: so in the source; the text appears disturbed here, since it explains the accusative نَزَّاعَةً and then names the nominative نَزَّاعَةٌ as the predicate.]» And if you wish, you make ﴿لَظَى﴾ nominative as the khabar of ﴿إِنَّ﴾ and make "النزّاعة" nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).

akhfash:19-19.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً﴾, then He said ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ﴾: He made ﴿الإِنْسانَ﴾ a plurality, and what shows you this is that He has excepted a plurality from it.

akhfash:36-37.t: And He said ﴿فَمَالِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ قِبَلَكَ مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ عِزِينَ﴾, just as you say "ما لَكَ قَائِماً" ("why are you standing?"). The singular of "العِزِينَ" is العِزَةُ (a band), like "ثُبَة" and "ثُبِين".

daas-irab:1-3.t: ﴿سَأَلَ سائِلٌ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِعَذابٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿واقِعٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of عذاب; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿لِلْكافِرينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to سأل. ﴿لَيْسَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of laysa. ﴿دافِعٌ﴾ the postponed noun of laysa; the clause is a second adjective of عذاب. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to واقع. ﴿ذِي﴾ an adjective of the Name of Majesty (Allah). ﴿الْمَعارِجِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿تَعْرُجُ الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَالرُّوحُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فِي يَوْمٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to something omitted, its implied form being «occurs» (يقع). ﴿كانَ مِقْدارُهُ خَمْسِينَ﴾ kāna, its noun and its predicate. ﴿أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾ tamyīz (specification), annexed to سنة; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of يوم.

daas-irab:5-7.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ صَبْراً﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿جَمِيلًا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿يَرَوْنَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the hāʾ is its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بَعِيداً﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَنَراهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿قَرِيباً﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:8-10.t: ﴿يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السَّماءُ﴾ an adverb of time, and a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb and its noun. ﴿كَالْمُهْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of تكون; المهل: molten silver; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَتَكُونُ الْجِبالُ كَالْعِهْنِ﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf); العهن is wool. ﴿وَلا يَسْئَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيماً﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the second object is omitted, its implied form being «his intercession» (شفاعته); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the hāʾ is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of حميما. ﴿يَوَدُّ الْمُجْرِمُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لَوْ يَفْتَدِي﴾ law is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar formed from law and the verb is the object of يود. ﴿مِنْ عَذابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿يَوْمِئِذٍ﴾ يوم is an adverb of time annexed to its like. ﴿بِبَنِيهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يفتدي.

daas-irab:12-14.t: ﴿وَصاحِبَتِهِ وَأَخِيهِ﴾ both conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes them. ﴿وَفَصِيلَتِهِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ a relative noun, an adjective (ṣifa) of فصيلته. ﴿تُؤْوِيهِ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ conjoined to بنيه. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ثُمَّ يُنْجِيهِ﴾ thumma is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:15-18.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr). ﴿إِنَّها﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَظى﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿نَزَّاعَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لِلشَّوى﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نزاعة; الشوى is the plural of شواة, the skin of the head. ﴿تَدْعُوا﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿أَدْبَرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أدبر, and what follows it is conjoined to it.

daas-irab:19-21.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿خُلِقَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿هَلُوعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿إِذا مَسَّهُ﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive, and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الشَّرُّ﴾ its fāʿil (agent). ﴿جَزُوعاً﴾ khabar of an omitted kāna, omitted together with its noun; the omitted clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position, and the clause مسه is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَإِذا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعاً﴾ the verse is conjoined (maʿṭūf).

daas-irab:22-23.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿الْمُصَلِّينَ﴾ excepted (mustathnā), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ badal (substitute) of المصلين. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿دائِمُونَ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين.

daas-irab:24-25.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding الذين. ﴿فِي أَمْوالِهِمْ حَقٌّ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate) and a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مَعْلُومٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿لِلسَّائِلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) معلوم. ﴿وَالْمَحْرُومِ﴾ conjoined to السائل.

daas-irab:26-28.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding الذين. ﴿يُصَدِّقُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿بِيَوْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الدِّينِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ also conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْ عَذابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to مشفقون. ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿إِنَّ عَذابَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿غَيْرُ﴾ khabar of inna. ﴿مَأْمُونٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:29-29.t: The i'rab of its like has preceded in verse 27. [Translator's note: so in the source.]

daas-irab:30-30.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿عَلى أَزْواجِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) حافظون. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿ما﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أزواجهم. ﴿مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation (taʿlīl), and inna, its noun and its predicate, which is annexed to ملومين; the nominal clause is causal.

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿فَمَنِ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿من﴾ a conditional noun as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿ابْتَغى﴾ a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿وَراءَ ذلِكَ﴾ an adverb of place, and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾ the fāʾ occurring in the apodosis of the condition. ﴿أولئك﴾ a demonstrative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿العادُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of the condition are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من.

daas-irab:32-32.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لِأَماناتِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) راعون. ﴿وَعَهْدِهِمْ﴾ conjoined to أماناتهم. ﴿راعُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:33-33.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun, also conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بِشَهاداتِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them. ﴿قائِمُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:34-34.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to its like in the preceding verses. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them. ﴿يُحافِظُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:35-35.t: ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ the demonstrative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِي جَنَّاتٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿مُكْرَمُونَ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:36-37.t: ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لِ الَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿قِبَلَكَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); مهطعين means: keeping their gaze fixed. ﴿عَنِ الْيَمِينِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَعَنِ الشِّمالِ﴾ both conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes them. ﴿عِزِينَ﴾ ḥāl; عزين means: in groups, circle upon circle.

daas-irab:38-38.t: ﴿أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving, rebuking interrogation, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), which is annexed to امرئ. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of امرئ. ﴿أَنْ يُدْخَلَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿جَنَّةَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿نَعِيمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to the verb يطمع; the clause «أيطمع..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:39-39.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr). ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿خَلَقْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلقناهم. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما.

daas-irab:40-40.t: ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿لا أُقْسِمُ﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِرَبِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْمَشارِقِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالْمَغارِبِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَقادِرُونَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿قادرون﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:41-41.t: ﴿عَلى أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ﴾ a preposition, and an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by ʿalā, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) قادرون. ﴿خَيْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خيرا. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is of ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ما﴾ the Ḥijāzī negative mā. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ its noun. ﴿بِمَسْبُوقِينَ﴾ genitive in form by the redundant (zāʾida) bāʾ, accusative in position as the khabar (predicate) of mā; the nominal clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:42-42.t: ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَخُوضُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿وَيَلْعَبُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يخوضوا. ﴿حَتَّى يُلاقُوا﴾ ḥattā is a particle of limit and a preposition, and an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after ḥattā, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿يَوْمَهُمُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by ḥattā, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يلعبوا. ﴿يُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:43-43.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ﴾ badal (substitute) of يومهم, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿مِنَ الْأَجْداثِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿سِراعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ﴾ kaʾanna and its noun. ﴿إِلى نُصُبٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what follows them. ﴿يُوفِضُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; يوفضون: they hasten; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of kaʾanna, and the nominal clause is a second ḥāl.

daas-irab:44-44.t: ﴿خاشِعَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَبْصارُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil (agent) of خاشعة. ﴿تَرْهَقُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ذِلَّةٌ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; the verbal clause is a second ḥāl. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ the demonstrative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْيَوْمُ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of اليوم. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause «كانوا..» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿سَأَلَ سَآئِلٌ﴾.
A caller called for a punishment bound to fall. He was al-Naḍr [ibn al-Ḥārith] ibn Kalada; he said: O Allah, if what Muḥammad says is the truth from You, then rain stones upon us from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment. He was taken captive on the day of Badr and was executed in bonds (ṣabran), he and ʿUqba.
His saying: ﴿بِعَذَابٍ وَاقِعٍ﴾.
He means: for the unbelievers. الواقع is an adjective (naʿt) of العذاب, and the lām in الكافرين is attached to العذاب, not to الواقع.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿ولا يَسْأَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيماً﴾.
A relative will not ask about his relative; but they are made to recognise them [in the passive voice] for an hour, and then there is no mutual recognition after that hour. Some read: (ولا يُسْأَلُ حَميمٌ حَمِيماً): a close friend will not be asked: Where is your friend? I do not favour that, because it goes against the interpretation, and because the readers are agreed on (يَسأَل).

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿وَفَصِيلَتِهِ﴾: it is the smallest [i.e. nearest] of his ancestral lines, the one to which he traces his descent.

farraa:14-15.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ﴾, that is: [that] the ransom might save him from Allah's punishment.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿كَلاَّ﴾, that is: that will not save him. Then He began afresh and said: ﴿إِنَّهَا لَظَىٰ﴾. Laẓā is one of the names of Hell; for that reason He did not make it fully declinable (lam yujrihi).

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿نَزَّاعَةٌ لِّلشَّوَىٰ﴾.
It is nominative according to your saying: إنها لظى، إنها نزاعة للشوى (it is Laẓā; it is a stripper-off of the scalp). Or, if you wish, you may make the هاء a support pronoun (ʿimād), and make لظى nominative by نزاعة and نزاعة by لظى, as you say in speech: إِنَّه جاريتُك فارهة and إنها جاريتُك فارهة (your slave-girl is lively). The هاء in both ways is ʿimād. الشَّوَى are the hands and the feet; the scalp is called شواة; and whatever is not a fatal spot is شوًى.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿تَدْعُو مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ﴾.
It says to the unbeliever: O unbeliever, to me! O hypocrite, to me! So it calls each one by his name.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰ﴾.
He is saying: he gathered and hoarded — put it in a container (wiʿāʾ) — and paid no zakat from it and did not maintain ties of kinship.

farraa:19-22.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً﴾.
الهلوع is the impatient, and his description is as Allah said: ﴿إِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ جَزُوعاً﴾ ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلْخَيْرُ مَنُوعاً﴾; this is the description of the هلوع. From it one says: هلِع يهلَع هلَعاً, like جزِع يجزَع جزعا. Then He said: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ﴾, excepting those who pray from الإنسان, because الإنسان is in the sense of a plural, as Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّ الإِنْسَانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ، إِلاَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿حَقٌّ مَعْلُومٌ﴾.
[It is] the zakat. Some said: No, rather it is something other than the zakat.

farraa:29-30.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ عَلَىٰ أَزْوَاجِهِمْ﴾.
Someone may ask: Is it permissible in speech to say: مررت بالقوم إِلاَّ بزيد (I passed by the people except by Zayd), meaning: except that I did not pass by Zayd? I said: That is not permissible; but what is in the Book of Allah is correct and good, because the beginning of the statement there is like a prohibition, since it was mentioned: ﴿والَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُون﴾. He is saying: they are not blamed except with regard to those other than their wives; so the statement proceeds according to ملومين at its end. Similar to it is your saying to a man: Do what you like except [for] killing a soul, for you will be punished — or: [except] in killing a soul; its meaning is: except that you will be punished for killing a soul.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿ذِي ٱلْمَعَارِجِ﴾.
It is an attribute of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because the angels ascend to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; so He described Himself by that.

farraa:37-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ عِزِينَ﴾.
العزون are circles, groups. They used to gather around the Prophet ﷺ and say: If these enter Paradise, as Muḥammad ﷺ says, we will surely enter it before them, and we will surely have more in it than they have. So Allah sent down: ﴿أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِىءٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ﴾.
The people read: "أن يُدخَل", with its agent unnamed (i.e. passive) [217/a]; and al-Ḥasan read: "أن يَدخُلَ", assigning the verb to him. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear and said [in effect]: Why do they despise them, when We created them all "from what they know" — from dust?

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾.
He is saying: if others than the angels were to ascend, they would ascend in the span of fifty thousand years. As for (يعرج), the readers are agreed on tāʾ [تعرج]. One of the shaykhs mentioned, from Zuhayr, from Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh read "يعرج" with yāʾ. And al-Aʿmash said: I have never heard anyone read it except with tāʾ. Both are correct.

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ﴾. الإيفاض is hastening. The poet said:
لأنْعتنْ نعامةً ميفاضا * خَرْجاءَ ظلت تطلبُ الإضاضَا
(I will surely describe a swift ostrich, of two colours, that kept seeking a refuge.)
He said: خرجاء refers to colour: when a white shirt is patched with a red patch, it is أخرج. تطلب الإضاضا: i.e. she seeks a place to enter and take refuge in. Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read: "إلى نَصْبٍ": to something set up, towards which they race. Zayd ibn Thābit read: "إلى نُصُب يوفضون", as if النُّصُب were the gods that were worshipped [besides Allah]. Both are correct, and it is a singular; the plural is أنصاب.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُ بَعِيداً﴾.
He means the Resurrection; and We see it as near, because everything that is coming is near.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Maʿārij
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿سَألَ سائِلٌ بِعَذابٍ واقِعٍ﴾ ("A questioner asked for a punishment bound to fall"). It was also read «سالَ» without hamza. One says «سَألْتُ، أسْألُ» and «سَلْتُ، أسالُ», and «الرَّجُلانِ يَتَساءَلانِ» and «يَتَساوَلانِ» ("the two men ask each other") with one meaning. The interpretation is: "A caller called for a punishment bound to fall", and that is like their saying: ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كانَ هَذا هو الحَقَّ مِن عِنْدِكَ فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ أوِ ائْتِنا بِعَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32] ("O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain stones upon us from the sky or bring us a painful punishment"). It was also said that the meaning of «سَألَ سائِلٌ بِعَذابٍ» is: [he asked] about a punishment bound to fall, and the answer is His saying: ﴿لِلْكافِرِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُ دافِعٌ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 2] ("for the unbelievers; there is none to avert it"), i.e. it will fall upon the unbelievers. And it was said that in «سالَ سايِلٌ» without hamza, «سايِل» is a valley in Hell.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَلا يَسْألُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمًا﴾ ("And no close friend will ask about a close friend"). It was also read «وَلا يُسْألُ حَمِيمٌ» ("no close friend will be asked [about]"). Whoever reads «وَلا يَسْألُ», the meaning is that they recognise one another, and what indicates it is His saying ﴿يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 11] ("they will be shown them"). Whoever reads «وَلا يُسْألُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمًا», the meaning is: "No relative will be asked about his kin", and ﴿يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 11] — and Allah knows best — would refer to the angels.

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿وَفَصِيلَتِهِ الَّتِي تُؤْوِيهِ﴾ ("and his clan that sheltered him") means: the nearest of his tribe to him.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿كَلا إنَّها لَظى﴾ ("No! Indeed, it is Laẓā"): «كَلّا» is a deterrent and a warning, i.e. "None of these will return, so take heed."

zajjaj:16-16.t:
It was read ﴿نَـزّاعَةً لِلشَّوى﴾ ("plucking off the extremities", accusative), while the [established] reading is «نَزّاعَةٌ» (nominative), and the readers follow it; in grammar it is stronger than the accusative. Abū ʿUbayd mentioned that it [the accusative] is permissible in Arabic, and that he did not know anyone who read it so. It has been narrated from al-Ḥasan, and there is disagreement about it from ʿĀṣim: what Abū ʿAmr narrated from ʿĀṣim is ﴿نَـزّاعَةً﴾ in the accusative, while others narrated «نَزّاعَةٌ» in the nominative.
As for the nominative, it is from three angles. One of them is that «لَظى» and «نَزّاعَة» are both the khabar (predicate) of the hāʾ and alif [of «إنَّها»], as you say «إنَّهُ حُلْوٌ حامِضٌ» ("it is sweet-sour"), meaning that it combines both tastes; the hāʾ and alif would then be a pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa) — what the Kufans call "the unknown (al-majhūl)" — and the meaning is: "the story and the matter is: Laẓā, plucking off the extremities." «الشَّوى» are the extremities: the two hands, the two feet and the head; and «الشَّوى» is the plural of «شَواة», which is the skin of the head. The poet said:
؎قالَتْ قُتَيْلَةُ ما لَهُ ∗∗∗ قَدْ جُلِّلَتْ شَيْبًا شَواتُهْ؟
(Qutayla said: What is the matter with him, his scalp all covered in grey?)
As for the accusative of ﴿نَـزّاعَةً﴾, it is as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of emphasis (ḥāl muʾakkida), as He said: ﴿وَهُوَ الحَقُّ مُصَدِّقًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 91] ("while it is the truth, confirming"), and as you say «أنا زَيْدٌ مَعْرُوفًا» ("I am Zayd, well known"); so ﴿نَـزّاعَةً﴾ is accusative, emphasising the matter of the Fire. It may also be accusative on the meaning that it blazes (tatalaẓẓā) as one that plucks off, as He, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿فَأنْذَرْتُكم نارًا تَلَظّى﴾ [al-Layl: 14] ("So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes"). The third angle for the nominative: it is nominative as [an expression of] censure (dhamm), with an implied «هِيَ», in the sense: "it is one that plucks off the extremities." Its accusative may also be as censure, so its accusative is on three angles.
[Translator's note: the text announces three angles for the nominative but, between the first and the "third", gives the accusative analyses; the second nominative angle is not stated explicitly. Translated as written.]

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿تَدْعُو مَن أدْبَرَ وتَوَلّى﴾ ("It calls whoever turned his back and went away"): it calls the unbeliever by his name and the hypocrite by his name.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا﴾ ("Indeed, man was created anxious"): «الهَلُوع», according to the explanation contained in the verse [itself], is one who is frightened and impatient at evil.

zajjaj:20-20.t: ﴿إذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ جَزُوعًا﴾ ﴿وَإذا مَسَّهُ الخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 21] ("When evil touches him, impatient; and when good touches him, withholding"). «الإنْسان» here has the meaning of "people", so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made an exception of the believers who pray, saying: ﴿إلا المُصَلِّينَ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 22] ﴿الَّذِينَ هم عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ دائِمُونَ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 23] ("except those who pray, who are constant in their prayer"): He means by it those who keep up the prescribed prayer. It is also possible that it means "those who do not turn their faces away from the direction of the qibla and do not look around", so that its derivation would be from «الدّائِم», which is the still — as the prohibition has come against urinating in still (dāʾim) water. And «المَحْرُوم» ("the deprived") is the one who is luckless, who has been deprived of earnings and does not ask.

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حافِظُونَ﴾ ﴿إلا عَلى أزْواجِهِمْ أوْ ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُهم فَإنَّهم غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 30] ("And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for they are not to be blamed"), i.e. with respect to these. It was said that it [«عَلى»] has the meaning of «مِن»; the meaning according to the one who says this is: "except from their wives or those their right hands possess". And it was said that «عَلى» is construed according to the sense, the meaning being: "for they are not blamed regarding their wives", and what indicates this is ﴿فَإنَّهم غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 30].

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿ذِي المَعارِجِ﴾ ("Owner of the ways of ascent"): it was said: "the ascending stairways of the angels"; and it was said: "Owner of the [heavenly] bounties (fawāḍil)".
[Translator's note: the source prints «ذِي الفَواصِلِ»; the usual gloss is «ذِي الفَواضِلِ» ("Owner of bounties"), so this is probably a misprint. Translated in that sense.]

zajjaj:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ العادُونَ﴾ ("then those are the transgressors"): its meaning is in [the sense of] ʿudwān (aggression), which is going to extremes in opposing Allah's command and exceeding the measure in wrongdoing. And it was said: ﴿فَمَنِ ابْتَغى وراءَ ذَلِكَ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ العادُونَ﴾ ("So whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors"), i.e. whoever seeks other than wives and those whom the right hands possess has transgressed. «العادُون» is the plural of «عادٍ», [plural] «عادُونَ».

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم لأماناتِهِمْ وعَهْدِهِمْ راعُونَ﴾ ("And those who are keepers of their trusts and their covenant"), i.e. they observe the covenant and the trust and safeguard them. Everyone who safeguards something is an observer (murāʿin) of it, and the leader is a shepherd (rāʿin) of his flock.

zajjaj:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿فَمالِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قِبَلَكَ مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ ("So what is the matter with those who disbelieve, hastening towards you with fixed gaze?"): «مُهْطِعِينَ» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «المُهْطِع» is one who directs his gaze at a thing and does not leave it, because they used to look at the Prophet (peace be upon him) with a look of enmity. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَتَراهم يَنْظُرُونَ إلَيْكَ وهم لا يُبْصِرُونَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 198] ("And you see them looking at you while they do not see"); its meaning is: [looking] in rage and resentment.

zajjaj:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿عَنِ اليَمِينِ وعَنِ الشِّمالِ عِزِينَ﴾ ("on the right and on the left, in separate groups"): circle by circle, group by group. «عِزِينَ» is the plural of «عِزَة». They were gathered on his right and his left, and they said: "If Muḥammad's companions enter Paradise, we shall enter it before them, and if they are given something in it, we shall be given more than that." So He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿أيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِنهم أنْ يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 38] ("Does every man among them aspire to be admitted to a Garden of bliss?"); it was also read «أنْ يَدْخُلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ» ("to enter a Garden of bliss"). Then He said: ﴿كَلا إنّا خَلَقْناهم مِمّا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 39] ("No! Indeed, We created them from what they know"), i.e. from dust and from a drop of sperm — so what do they have by which they would be admitted to Paradise, while they persist in enmity and hatred towards you?!

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿تَعْرُجُ المَلائِكَةُ والرُّوحُ إلَيْهِ في يَوْمٍ كانَ مِقْدارُهُ خَمْسِينَ ألْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾ ("The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years"). It has come in the exegesis that it is the Day of Resurrection; and it has also come that its measure, were you to undertake it, would be fifty thousand years, whereas the angels ascend in every single day. It was read «تَعْرُجُ المَلائِكَةُ» and «يَعْرُجُ المَلائِكَةُ». It was also said: from the first of the days of this world until its end is fifty thousand years. And it is possible that «فِي يَوْمٍ» belongs to (is attached to) «واقِعٍ», so the meaning would be: "A questioner asked for a punishment bound to fall on a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years", and that punishment falls on the Day of Resurrection.

zajjaj:40-41.t: His saying: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ المَشارِقِ والمَغارِبِ إنّا لَقادِرُونَ﴾ ﴿عَلى أنْ نُبَدِّلَ خَيْرًا مِنهُمْ﴾ ("So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests that We are able to replace them with better than them"). Its meaning is: "So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests", and «لا» is emphatic, as He said: ﴿لِئَلا يَعْلَمَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 29], whose meaning is "so that the People of the Book may know". The meaning of ﴿بِرَبِّ المَشارِقِ والمَغارِبِ﴾ is: the rising-places of the sun and its setting-places, and likewise of the moon; these are the rising-places of summer and of winter and the setting-places of summer and of winter. The sun rises each day from a [different] rising-place and sets in a [different] setting-place, and likewise the moon.

zajjaj:42-42.t: His saying: ﴿فَذَرْهم يَخُوضُوا ويَلْعَبُوا حَتّى يُلاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ﴾ ("So leave them to indulge and play until they meet their Day which they are promised"): «يَخُوضُوا» is the answer to the imperative, jussive (majzūm). It was also said that it is jussive, even though its wording lacks the particle of command, because it was put in the place of the imperative, as if He said: «لِيَخُوضُوا ولِيَلْعَبُوا» ("let them indulge and let them play"). This is a command by way of threat, as you say: "Do what you like, for I shall punish you for it." The explanation of this has already been given exhaustively.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الأجْداثِ سِراعًا كَأنَّهم إلى نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ﴾ ("The Day they will come out of the graves rapidly, as if racing to a nuṣub"). «الأجْداث» are the graves; their singular is «جَدَث», and «جَدَف» is also said with this meaning. It was read «إلى نَصْبٍ يُوفِضُونَ» and «إلى نُصْبٍ» with ḍamma on the nūn and sukūn on the ṣād, and it was read ﴿إلى نُصُبٍ﴾ with ḍamma on the nūn and the ṣād. Whoever reads «نَصْبٍ», its meaning is: "as if [racing] to a marker set up (manṣūb) for them…"; and whoever reads «إلى نُصْبٍ», its meaning is: "to idols of theirs…", as He said: ﴿وَما ذُبِحَ عَلى النُّصُبِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 3] ("and what is slaughtered on stone altars"). The meaning of ﴿يُوفِضُونَ﴾ is: they hasten. The poet said:
؎لَأنْعَتَنَّ نَعامَةً مِيفاضًا ∗∗∗ خَرْجاءَ تَغْدُو وتَطْلُبُ الأضّاضا
(I shall surely describe a swift ostrich, pied black and white, running off at dawn and seeking a refuge.)
«المِيفاض» is the swift one; «خَرْجاء» is one of two colours, black and white; and the meaning of «الأضّاض» is the place in which refuge is sought; one says «أضَتْنِي إلَيْكَ الحاجَةُ أضاضًا» ("need has driven me to you").

zajjaj:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿تَرْهَقُهم ذِلَّةٌ﴾ ("abasement will cover them"), i.e. abasement will overspread them.
And His saying: ﴿مِن عَذابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 11] ("from the punishment of that Day") was read with fatḥa and with kasra. Whoever reads «يَوْمِ» with kasra does so on the basic rule of annexation (iḍāfa), because the word to which the first is annexed is genitive (majrūr) by annexation. Whoever reads «يَوْمَ» with fatḥa does so because it is annexed to something non-declinable (ghayr mutamakkin) — annexed to «إذْ», and «إذْ» is vague (mubhama); its meaning is "the day when such-and-such happens". Since it is vague and [the noun] is annexed to it, the word annexed to it was made indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa. In the same way they recited the poet's saying:
؎لَمْ يَمْنَعِ الشُّرْبَ مِنها غَيْرَ أنْ نَطَقَتْ ∗∗∗ حَمامَةٌ في غُصُونٍ ذاتِ أوْقالِ
(Nothing prevented her from drinking except that a dove cooed among branches laden with fruit.)
When he annexed «غَيْرَ» to «أنْ», he made it indeclinable on fatḥa, though it is in the position of a nominative. The nominative has also been narrated: they said «غَيْرُ أنْ نَطَقَتْ», just as the word [in the verse] was read with the genitive inflection and with indeclinability on fatḥa.

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فاصْبِرْ صَبْرًا جَمِيلا﴾ ("So be patient with a beautiful patience"): this indicates that it was before the Prophet (peace be upon him) was commanded to fight.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّهم يَرَوْنَهُ بَعِيدًا﴾ ﴿وَنَراهُ قَرِيبًا﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 7] ("Indeed, they see it as far off, but We see it as near"): they see it as far off in their view, as though they consider it remote in the sense of [its being] impossible, just as you say to your opponent in debate: "This is far-fetched; it cannot be."

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿وَنَراهُ قَرِيبًا﴾ ("but We see it as near"), i.e. sound, its like being easy to understand through the way Allah has given evidence for the Day of Raising by His saying ﴿قُلْ يُحْيِيها الَّذِي أنْشَأها أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 79] ("Say: He will give them life who produced them the first time"), and similar arguments concerning the raising.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السَّماءُ كالمُهْلِ﴾ ﴿وَتَكُونُ الجِبالُ كالعِهْنِ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 9] ("The Day the sky will be like muhl, and the mountains like ʿihn"): «العِهْن» is wool, and «المُهْل» is the dregs of oil.
